_readme: WHICH FEATURE IS IN WHICH CHANNEL, IN THE RIDER'S WORDS.
docs/channels.md is the author. This is its machine-readable twin: the same beta and
dev rows, the same section title, in a form a Python verifier can read.
Pinned from both sides. The kit's ChannelFeatures (Help/ChannelFeatures.swift) is
asserted equal to `sectionTitle`, `beta[].text` and `dev[].text` by CopyContractTests;
the web's two lists are asserted equal to the same rows by the web verifier. Edit
docs/channels.md first, then this file and the kit together.
`id` is a slug that outlives a rewording, so the web can pin one row while its sentence
changes. COPY_WRITE=1 replaces the texts by position and leaves the ids alone.
`forbiddenInRelease` is the guard on the release copy, not a list of rows: no release
text may contain any of these, case-insensitively, as a substring. See README.md.

beta.text: .gpx and .tcx files, so a session exported from a Polar, a Suunto or a COROS opens straight from Files.
Apple Health, both ways: what Apple's Workout app recorded is read in, and your sessions are written back as workouts.
The CleanJibe Apple Watch app, which records on your wrist with live numbers and hands the session to the phone.
Home-screen widgets and the watch complication.
The session video: your afternoon as a film rather than a card.
Grouping the library by month, year or spot, and filtering it.
Planned: a live view on the Apple Watch. Foil state, flights, records and turn verdicts on the wrist, as the Garmin app shows them.

dev.text: The Garmin link: a summary card from your watch the moment you stop. Your spot's map and the wind direction go back to it.
Windsurf, foil and fin, with thresholds of its own
The tuning page: every analysis threshold on a slider, tried against your own sessions
